turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Patrick Allen. Date of birth: 7/7/1977. New patient visit. Past medical history includes gerd, anxiety, depression. Here for chronic abdominal pain. He had an abdominal ct on 1/23/2020. Impression is a normal ct of the ab- abdomen. Hello, are you mr. Allen?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I am.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hi. My name is dr. Edwards. Nice to meet you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nice to meet you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Welcome to the gi specialty clinic.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Did you have any problems finding us?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've been here with my sister once before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Good. So how can I help you today? Uh, the referral I have is for abdominal pain and diarrhea.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Right. So I've had... I've been having this pain right here in my stomach, like right around here.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So in the area of your mid abdomen, just below the belly button?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Correct. I've had the pain on and off for about two years. I finally went to the er and a... A few months ago and they did a ct scan.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I saw that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah. They said they didn't really see anything on the scan.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yes, I agree. It looked normal.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The problem is I'm either constipated or have explosive diarrhea.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Is the pain there all the time?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's a nagging feeling and it just depends. Sometimes it bothers me, sometimes it doesn't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Has this been the case over the past two years as well?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: More recently in the past couple months, at least with the constipation and diarrhea.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And before that, how are your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: They were normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Uh, okay. So any blood in your stool?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Do you feel like you have more constipation or diarrhea?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably more constipation.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so when you're constipated, do you not have a bowel movement or is the stool hard?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I usually don't go, but when I do, it's hard.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how often do you have a bowel movement when you are constipated?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: About three to four times a week. It's like when I need to go to the bathroom, if I can massage it, it feels like it's moving some and I can eventually go.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And when you have a bowel movement, does the pain change?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, it gets a little better.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And are you eating and drinking okay? Any nausea or vomiting, heartburn or indigestion?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: None of that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. So tell me about the diarrhea, how often do you get it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It kinda just depends on what I eat. I think I have a very sensitive stomach. If I eat pasta with a creamy sauce, I'm probably gon na have diarrhea.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And it doesn't happen for multiple days in a row or is it just one time?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's usually just one time and then it's over.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how's your weight been? Any fluctuation?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nice and pretty stable, although I could stand to lose about 25 pounds.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And is there any family history of gi issues that you know of?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not that I can think of. Well, actually my sister does have problems with her stomach too. She has irritable bowel syndrome and that is kind of what I always thought I had even thought I've never been diagnosed with it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And is there any family history of gi cancer or liver disease?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you ever had any surgeries on your abdomen?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've never had any surgery.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, so your gallbladder, appendix, all those are still intact?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yup.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you ever had a colonoscopy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No. I thought that happen when you turn 50.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, that's for colon cancer screening, but there are other reasons to have a colonoscopy, like unexplained abdominal pain and changes in bowel habits.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, come have a seat here and lay back so I can examine you.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I'm gon na start by listening to your belly with my steth- stethoscope. And I hear bowel sounds in all four quadrants.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: What does that mean? Is everything okay?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: It just means that I can hear little noises in all areas of your belly, which means your bowels are active and working.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay, good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So now, I'm going to push on your upper and lower abdomen. Let me know if you have any pain.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It hurts a little when you push right there on the left side, near my belly button.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. I do feel stool in your lower colon, which would coincide with constipation, but I also feel a slight enlargement of your liver here on the upper right side. Have you had any lab work done recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I have a physical about four months ago and they... I had blood drawn then.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And did your primary care physician say anything about the lab results?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: He said I had some very slightly elevated liver enzymes, but we would recheck them in about six months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And you remember what enzymes were elevated, alt, ast, alp?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: He said the alt and the ast were elevated.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you take any medications, either prescription or over-the-counter?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I take crestor and olmesartan daily and then tylenol for occasion- occasional pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how frequently do you take the tylenol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hardly ever. Maybe once a month.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you consume alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yes, but only a couple of beers after working in the yard on saturdays.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And no previous history of heavy alcohol or drug use?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you had any recent issues with excessive bruising or bleeding?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nope.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about any issues with your ankles or feet swelling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. I'm gon na take a look at your eyes and skin. I don't see any jaundice.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: What would cause that?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Issues with your liver. Let me take a quick listen to your heart and lungs.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Lungs are clear, bilateral heart sounds are normal, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs noted.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That's good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yes. The rest of your physical exam is normal other than what seems to be an increased stool burden in your colon and a slight hepatomegaly.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: What's that?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Increase stool burden means that there's a lot of stool sitting in your colon.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: And that's the constipation, right? But what about the other thing?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: The hepatomegaly means the liver is enlarged.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: But you said mine was slightly enlarged?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Correct.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So what does that mean?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, let's talk about what we found and then some possible next steps if you're in agreement.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So as I said, the hepatomegaly means your liver is enlarged.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Could that be why my stomach is hurting and I'm having issues with the constipation and diarrhea?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, I think you're constipated and have occasional bouts of diarrhea because of certain foods you eat. And we can get you started right away on a fiber supplement that should help with that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So what about my liver? Why is it enlarged?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, there are many reasons why people can have an elevated liver enzymes and also enlarged liver. Some possible causes are certain medications that can be toxic to liver, alcohol abuse, fatty liver disease, hepatitis, cirrhosis, and other liver diseases like wilson's disease.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So what do I need to do?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Well, I think since it's been about four months since your blood work was done, we should check your liver enzymes in addition to a few other labs.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. And then what?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: We will get those drawn today and then depending upon the results you may need an ultrasound of your liver. I think we need to talk about your medications too.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Which medications?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Crestor, how long have you been taking that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: About 18 months.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Well, crestor is one of the medications that can cause liver toxicity so it may be a good idea to discuss other alternatives.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Should I talk to my primary care or can you change it?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I would recommend calling your primary care and discuss that with him since he follows you for your blood pressure and cholesterol.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. I'll call him this afternoon.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great. I also think we should go ahead and get you scheduled for a liver ultrasound. If your blood work looks good, then we can always cancel that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. When do you think I'll be able to get the ultrasound done?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hopefully, within the next two weeks. You will receive a call from the radiology scheduling this afternoon to get it set up.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. And then what happens?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: When I get the results from the test, I will contact you. And depending upon what we find, we'll come up with our next steps.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: And when should I see you again?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Uh, let's schedule an appointment when you check out to return in four weeks. We'll discuss how you're doing with the fiber supplement and your constipation and review test results to determine if we need to do further testing on your liver.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Is there anything else I can do to help with these issues?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Definitely refrain from drinking any alcohol, increase your water intake to at least 48 ounces a day in addition to taking the fiber supplement to help with your constipation. And be mindful of eating foods that you were sensitive to so you can avoid the bouts of diarrhea.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. And I'll talk to my primary care about my crestor.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Excellent. And do you have any other questions for me?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Great. So remember when you check out the front desk, schedule follow-up appointment with me for four weeks and then go to the lab to get your blood work drawn.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Okay. Sounds good.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And expect a call from radiology scheduling about setting up your ultrasound.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: All right. Thanks, dr. Edwards.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Thank you, mr. Allen.
